newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures fall after tankan report.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures fall after tankan report.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures fell on Wednesday morning after the Bank of Japan (BOJ) published its tankan survey of corporate sentiment.

"The tankan was as we had expected but it seemed to take some dealers by surprise," said one broker. "It wasn't received too well, and when it came out, the market sunk down to the morning low," he added.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract lost 125 points to reach a low of 17,705 and then recovered to stand at 17,770 by the lunchtime close.
Dealers said the Tokyo market had discounted most of the report's findings, which showed sentiment improving among big manufacturers but non-manufacturers more wary.
They said the new Japanese financial year, which began on April 1, had started slowly but most players expected more share buying to emerge gradually.
Technically the SIMEX Nikkei contract was said to be mvoing sideways across the chart.
"It's trying to build a bottom," said one analyst.
He said the contract had some support around 17,500 points and much stronger support either side of 17,000. On the upside, he saw resistance at 18,000 and 18,300.
"It will have a tough time breaking up through 18,300," the analyst added.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract stood at 336.3 by 0415 GMT against its opening at 336.9 on volume of 985 lots.
